arguments.court: US District Court, Eastern District of Texas
arguments.content:
MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT

I. INTRODUCTION
This action arises from a commercial dispute over an allegedly breached software licensing agreement between Meridian Technologies Inc. and Apex Global Solutions LLC. The damages claimed exceed $4.2 million, and jurisdiction is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1332 due to diversity of citizenship and amount in controversy.

II. LEGAL STANDARD
Under Fed. R. Civ. P. 56, summary judgment is appropriate where 'the movant shows that there is no genuine dispute as to any material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law.' See Celotex Corp. v. Catrett, 477 U.S. 317 (1986); Anderson v. Liberty Lobby, Inc., 477 U.S. 242 (1986). The moving party need not negate the opponent’s claim but must demonstrate the absence of a genuine issue of material fact.

III. ANALYSIS
A. Enforceability of Software Licensing Agreement
The licensing agreement at issue is governed by Texas law and falls within the scope of UCC Article 2 as interpreted in this jurisdiction. The contract contains a valid choice-of-law clause (Section 14.1) selecting Delaware law, which further supports enforceability.

B. Absence of Genuine Dispute
Defendant has failed to produce any admissible evidence creating a genuine factual dispute regarding material breach. The indemnification clause (Section 8.1) and limitation of liability (Section 8.3) were negotiated terms and do not render the contract unconscionable. Moreover, the non-compete clause (Section 12.1), while potentially overbroad, does not invalidate the entire agreement.

C. Precedent Supports Summary Judgment
In Celotex, the Supreme Court emphasized that the non-moving party must present more than mere allegations or denials. Here, Defendant's opposition lacks evidentiary support. Similarly, under Anderson, viewing all facts in the light most favorable to Defendant, no reasonable jury could find in its favor on the issue of breach.

IV. CONCLUSION
Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court grant summary judgment in its favor.

Respectfully submitted,
Smith & Associates LLP
Attorneys for Plaintiff
